cards.front: What must you watch for on an entrance ramp?
cards.back: You enter an interstate by an entrance ramp, paying careful attention to the signs because an exit ramp marked do not enter and wrong way often sits next to the entrance ramp, and advisory speed signs appear on ramps that curve sharply.

cards.front: What do you do about halfway along the entrance ramp?
cards.back: About halfway along the entrance ramp check the interstate traffic with quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, watch the vehicles ahead of you entering the acceleration lane, use your turn signal, and look for a gap in approaching traffic while adjusting your speed to meet it.

cards.front: How do you merge into interstate traffic?
cards.back: As you merge make sure you are traveling at the same speed as the other traffic, and do not cut sharply to the left into the traffic stream but follow the lane, merge, and only then change lanes.

cards.front: What do you do if a vehicle is ahead in the acceleration lane?
cards.back: If another vehicle is ahead of you in the acceleration lane be prepared for it to slow or stop without warning, and do not stop on the ramp or in the acceleration lane.

cards.front: What can you do if no gap is available?
cards.back: If no gap in traffic is available it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop, but because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous this maneuver is a last resort.

cards.front: Who has the right-of-way when you enter an interstate?
cards.back: Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way, and you cannot count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

cards.front: How do you prepare to exit an interstate?
cards.back: When exiting an interstate watch for the signs that show where your exit is and which lane to use, then signal and move into that lane well before the exit, because changing lanes at the last moment risks missing the exit or causing a crash.

cards.front: Where do you slow down when exiting?
cards.back: Most interstate exits have a deceleration lane for slowing before the exit ramp, so never slow down on the interstate itself but wait until you are in the deceleration lane and brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit.

cards.front: Where does braking for an exit belong?
cards.back: Braking for an exit belongs in the deceleration lane, never on the interstate itself, and the target is the posted exit ramp speed.

cards.front: Where is the last-resort stop when no gap appears?
cards.back: When no gap appears, the last-resort stop is on the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane, never on the ramp or in the acceleration lane itself.

cards.front: Who holds the right-of-way, and how does the entering driver merge?
cards.back: Traffic already on the interstate holds the right-of-way over entering traffic, so the entering driver matches speed, merges within the lane and only afterwards changes lanes rather than cutting sharply left.

cards.front: How is interstate driving different?
cards.back: Interstate and divided highways have largely removed the chance of head-on collisions, but interstate driving is very different and demands complete awareness of high-speed driving and constant alertness.

cards.front: How do you treat entering trucks and buses, and where does slower traffic drive?
cards.back: Trucks and buses entering an interstate may need extra time to adjust to the traffic pattern, so give them extra time and space, and slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane except when passing.
cards.memory_hook: Room for trucks, slow keep right

cards.front: What are interstate shoulders for?
cards.back: Interstate shoulders are only for disabled vehicles and must not be used for changing drivers, reading a map or other non-emergency purposes, which belong in a rest area or off the interstate.

cards.front: Why must you not stop in an exit gore?
cards.back: Do not stop in an exit gore, the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp, because a driver who missed the exit may try to cross the gore and strike your vehicle.

cards.front: Is parking allowed on interstate shoulders?
cards.back: No parking is permitted on the shoulders of interstates, and parked vehicles may be towed.

cards.front: What are the speed rules on an interstate?
cards.back: Never drive faster than the legal speed limit, do not drive slower than fifty-five miles per hour on an interstate unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, and always drive at a steady speed.

cards.front: Why is driving much slower than traffic hazardous, and which lane do you use?
cards.back: Driving much slower than other interstate drivers creates a hazard because others may be forced to change lanes abruptly, so always drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing another vehicle.

cards.front: What does state law require in adverse conditions, and how should you adjust?
cards.back: State law requires headlights to be turned on during adverse conditions, and in such conditions you should adjust your driving, keep an adequate following distance and adjust your speed to allow a safe stop.

cards.front: What are the interstate speed floor and ceiling, and which lane?
cards.back: The interstate floor is fifty-five miles per hour unless conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, the ceiling is always the legal limit, and the right lane is the place to be unless passing.

cards.front: How do the shoulder and exit gore rules differ?
cards.back: The shoulder is for disabled vehicles only and never for parking, while the exit gore between the through lane and the ramp is a place never to stop at all.

cards.front: How are interstates identified, and what do even and odd numbers mean?
cards.back: Interstate highways are identified by distinctive red, white and blue shields, even-numbered interstates run east to west, and odd-numbered interstates run north to south.

cards.front: What do three-digit interstate numbers mean?
cards.back: A three-digit interstate number whose first digit is even identifies a beltway or bypass around a city, while a three-digit number whose first digit is odd identifies a spur route.

cards.front: What should you plan and check before an interstate trip?
cards.back: Because interstate entrances and exits can be far apart, plan your route in advance and check gas, water, oil and tires including the spare before leaving, since a breakdown on an interstate costs time and can be dangerous.

cards.front: Why is the first interchange guide sign placed well ahead?
cards.back: On an interstate the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well before the point where you must turn off, giving time to change lanes and exit smoothly, so watch the guide signs to avoid hazardous last-minute maneuvers.

cards.front: How are added and removed through lanes shown?
cards.back: Where the number of through lanes changes, an added lane is usually obvious, while a removed lane usually ends at a fork or exit and is indicated by a black and yellow panel below the green and white overhead guide sign.

cards.front: What is an interchange, and what are the three common types?
cards.back: An interchange is the intersection of two highways at different levels, over and under, with separate connecting roads that let vehicles cross, enter or leave either road without interfering with others, and the three most common types are cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet.

cards.front: What direction do even and odd interstates run?
cards.back: An even interstate number means an east-west route while an odd number means a north-south route.

cards.front: How do three-digit numbers distinguish a bypass from a spur?
cards.back: A three-digit interstate number starting with an even digit is a beltway or bypass around a city, while one starting with an odd digit is a spur route.

cards.front: How are removed and added through lanes announced?
cards.back: A removed through lane is announced by a black and yellow panel beneath the green and white overhead guide sign, whereas an added lane is usually obvious without one.

cards.front: What are the three common interchange types?
cards.back: Cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet are the three common interchange types, and every interchange joins two highways at different levels with connecting roads.

cards.front: Who may use designated mobility impaired parking spaces?
cards.back: West Virginia law reserves designated parking spaces for mobility impaired citizens whose condition limits their ability to walk reasonable distances, and people who routinely transport mobility impaired persons may also use those spaces.

cards.front: How do you get a mobility impaired placard or plate, and what is the plate fee?
cards.back: To obtain a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate a doctor must certify the condition on a form the DMV provides, the DMV issues the placard or plate after approving the application, and the mobility impaired license plate carries a transfer fee of ten dollars and fifty cents.

cards.front: When is it illegal to park in a mobility impaired space?
cards.back: It is illegal to park a vehicle in a designated mobility impaired area unless it displays a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate.

cards.front: What should an applicant with a disability or medical problem include with the application?
cards.back: About one in every ten people has some disability, no single set of rules can judge every person's ability to drive safely, and an applicant with a physical disability or medical problem that may interfere with driving should prepare a letter explaining the situation to accompany the license application.

cards.front: Where can a driver get a list of adaptive aid manufacturers?
cards.back: A driver who needs adaptive aids such as hand controls can get a list of manufacturers from the driver's license examiner or from the Driver Education Department of the West Virginia Division of Rehabilitation Services.

cards.front: What does the DMV provide under the Americans with Disabilities Act?
cards.back: Under the Americans with Disabilities Act the DMV does not discriminate on the basis of disability, generally provides aids and services for effective communication on request, makes reasonable modifications to its policies, and welcomes service animals in its offices even where pets are prohibited.

cards.front: How far ahead must you request an aid or modification?
cards.back: Anyone who needs an auxiliary aid or a modification of DMV procedures should contact the DMV no later than forty-eight hours before the scheduled arrival.

cards.front: What is the DMV not required to do, and what will it not charge?
cards.back: The Americans with Disabilities Act does not require the DMV to fundamentally alter its programs or take on an undue financial or administrative burden, and the DMV will not place a surcharge on a person or group with disabilities to cover the cost of aids, services or modifications.

cards.front: Where do accessibility concerns go, and what is an example modification?
cards.back: Questions or concerns about accessibility go to the DMV's ADA coordinator, and reasonable modifications include retrieving items from public locations that are not accessible to people who use wheelchairs.

cards.front: What does a placard require, and what does the plate cost?
cards.back: A mobility impaired placard or plate requires a doctor's certification on the DMV form and the plate carries a ten dollar and fifty cent transfer fee, and parking in a designated space without displaying one is illegal.

cards.front: How far ahead is an accommodation request due, and who pays?
cards.back: An accommodation request to the DMV must arrive at least forty-eight hours before the visit, and the DMV may not charge the person with a disability for the aid or modification.

recap_hooks.text: Remember entrance ramp warnings, halfway up the ramp and match speed, then merge
Remember interstate driving demands alertness, room for trucks, slow keep right and shoulders for disabled vehicles
Remember even east-west, odd north-south, beltway versus spur numbers and plan and check before leaving
Remember mobility impaired parking spaces, getting a placard or plate and display placard to park
